scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The 'About This Report' section opens and sustains first-person voice ('We audited', 'We fetch', 'We then review'), but the 'Summary of Findings' closing section switches to first-person only in its final sentence while the rest of the report body uses first-person consistently — the real inconsistency is in the 'Findings' priority blocks, where Priorities 1–8 body paragraphs all use third-person passive constructions ('The pattern is consistent', 'The element carries no accessible name', 'Structured Data Quality scores') while the surrounding narrative sections use first-person ('We audited', 'We recommend', 'We invite the team').
findings.context: "Finding:** Across the audited set, every one of the 7 pages carries at least one anchor element"

findings.message: The 'Soft 404' check in the Agent Reading Pipeline section reports 'Pass · 7/7' with the finding 'Missing pages return a proper HTTP 404 status. No pages misleadingly return 200 for non-existent URLs', but the Discovery Files section explicitly documents that the site returns HTTP 200 soft-404s for at least 41 paths — the pipeline check's site-wide clean verdict contradicts the sample evidence and overstates the site's soft-404 handling.
findings.context: "Soft 404** - Pass · 7/7 … No pages misleadingly return 200 for non-existent URLs."

findings.message: The 'Optional Enhancements' section repeats 'sameAs links on Organisation' as an optional enhancement after it has already been identified and recommended with confidence as Priority 8 in the Findings section, creating an imbalance where the same evidenced gap is simultaneously asserted as a prioritised finding and downgraded to a discretionary enhancement.
findings.context: "sameAs links on Organisation: adding sameAs properties to the Organisation entities already present across the audited set"
